key_insight: Self-Privileged Fine-Tuning (SPFT) weights training tokens using a frozen initial model given privileged information, emphasizing tokens that are more predictive of the correct outcome.
engineering_relevance: SPFT offers a token-weighted supervised fine-tuning approach for improving mathematical reasoning and code generation.
method: Analyze induced targets: dynamic weighting heavily sharpens distributions, while static weighting combines the data distribution with a frozen prior.
Use a frozen initial model conditioned on privileged information, such as ground-truth answers, to generate token-level weights.
Apply these weights during fine-tuning; a Bayesian decomposition links the weighting to tokens' predictive value for the outcome.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improvements over standard SFT and other baselines across the main mathematical reasoning and code generation settings, without specifying benchmarks or effect sizes.
watch_item: Effectiveness depends on the quality of the privileged prior, and implementation requires generating token-level weights with a frozen model.
